subject: AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage

messages.author: 6e1a1d7d2508f1c9
messages.subject: AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage
parts:
Greetings,


I am attempting to fit a binomial space-time model using an AR1 latent model with a besag grouping model. Training data are entirely missing for significant stretches of the time series. There are 29 time points across which I want to make predictions, with data entirely absent for time points 2–10, 12–18, and 28–29.


The model is structured as follows:


y ~ -1 + b0 + f(ID.year, model = "ar1", replicate = as.integer(demo), 

    group = as.integer(as.factor(space_group)), control.group = list(model = "besag", graph = mat, scale.model = TRUE), values = unique(ID.year))


(“demo” refers to a demographic variable; I want separate estimates for each level of this variable, although this doesn’t seem to affect the behavior described below.)


The resulting model tracks the training data well but the temporal effects show surprising behavior in the years without data. I had expected that the model would show reasonable interpolation in the gap years, especially since rho is estimated to be high (0.991). However, the estimated temporal effects in gap years are always very high relative to the years with data. I suspect that this is related to the sum-to-zero constraint in the besag model, as an otherwise-identical model without the besag grouping model does not show the same behavior. Does this interpretation seem reasonable, and if so, is there a way around it? I have tried an RW1 model in place of AR1, and this works for small data subsets but struggles to fit our entire data set.


I seem to be unable to attach a screenshot to illustrate the problem, but am happy to share figures via email.


Thank you in advance for your assistance,


Chris Schmidt

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage
parts:
if you have missing time-points in the series, like

time=c(1,2,5,6,9)

and you want 1:9, then you need to add those in the 'values' argument

f(time, model="ar1", values=1:9)


which assign the 'values' for which the model is defined.


Let me know if this does no answer your question.

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] AR1-besag model with gaps in temporal coverage
parts:
I confirmed that the following model gives flat time series estimates, with a posterior mean for GroupRho of 0.001 (95%: -0.986, 0.986):

y ~ -1 + b0 + f(space_group, model = 'besag', replicate = as.integer(demo), graph = mat, group = as.integer(ID.year), control.group = list(model = 'ar1'), values = unique(space_group))

For both this and the original model described in the first post, I am using default priors. Do you see anything wrong with this specification?

Thank you,
Chris
